identity_bindings.input_title: Uncertainty Calibration Under Clustered Dependence and Segmentation Stress

rubric.instructions: Review the rendered pixels from one normal research-presentations production invocation. Check that each page contains source-specific content from the supplied engineering bundle rather than placeholders; exact CUHK Beamer identity is visible; the main scientific object is prominent and projection-readable; math, native plots, and medical images are semantically correct where present; no internal RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, workflow, repo path, run ID, or implementation language leaks into audience-facing slides; repeated generic cards or one-template pages are rejected; and the deck reads as one coherent research update rather than disconnected benchmark pages. For multi-workstream bundles, confirm that each workstream stays internally continuous and that any independent workstream transition is visible without inventing a causal relation. Separately review the deck_contact_sheet item as a deck-level rhythm object: adjacent-page density jumps, repeated composition face, overfull or empty pages, redundant summary filler, result -> failure -> next-experiment rhythm, workstream transition balance, and title/object/formula/image alternation must meet a mature doctoral group-meeting or strong conference-talk bar. The top-level package PASS is not enough; provide item-level judgement and observations for deck_contact_sheet. Do not infer visual quality from filenames or hashes.
source_contracts: The engineering regression bundle is public-safe and explicitly excluded from Stage 5 holdouts.
Stage 2 gold/reference pixels are used only for compatible composition selection.
The deck-quality loop may repair at most once and must fail closed/no-winner for unsafe findings or unresolved blockers.

observations: A large, projection-readable clustered-outcome equation is the central visual object.
The slide adds source-specific model components, random-effect interpretation, and the ICC expression rather than placeholder copy.
CUHK Beamer styling is visible through the purple navigation bar, crest, and footer treatment.
No audience-facing workflow, provenance, repository, run-ID, or implementation-language text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: Clear model setup slide with readable mathematics and specific statistical content.

observations: The three-panel coverage plot is native-looking and includes distinct G=8, G=20, and G=50 conditions, ICC values, method traces, target line, legend, and data-source statement.
The visual conclusion is legible: the red naive-iid coverage declines while the teal cluster-robust trace remains near nominal coverage.
Plot annotations and supporting interpretation are visually connected to the chart.
No placeholder, internal QA, or workflow text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: Specific quantitative result slide with a prominent, semantically coherent coverage plot.

observations: The design is presented as a left-to-right causal workflow from DGP knobs through clustered samples and interval procedures to diagnostics.
Cluster diagrams, procedure labels, and coverage diagnostics are distinct visual objects rather than generic repeated cards.
The connector caption explicitly explains the sequencing, making the experiment-design logic readable.
No forbidden internal-facing text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: A visually differentiated, readable simulation-design explanation that supports the surrounding results.

observations: The grouped bar chart visibly communicates the stated failure: cluster-robust coverage remains below the 0.95 target for the small-G setting.
Bar values, error bars, target line, and the “still below nominal” annotation make the negative result interpretable from the slide itself.
The adjacent explanatory text identifies the remaining CR2 and wild-cluster-bootstrap tests, linking failure evidence to the next step.
No internal RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, or implementation text is shown.
item_reviews.summary: The failure result is explicit, quantitatively supported, and usefully positioned before the next-experiment slide.

observations: The slide directly carries forward the prior small-G, ICC=.5, imbalance failure evidence into sampling manipulations, comparator arms, and a go/no-go decision rule.
The four-stage flow diagram is readable and uses distinct structures for evidence, alternatives, comparator bracket, and decision diamond.
The final criterion (“coverage >= .94 with controlled width”) is concrete rather than generic planning filler.
No internal workflow or implementation leakage is visible.
item_reviews.summary: A specific and visibly connected next-experiment plan.

observations: The slide visibly marks the workstream transition as “Segmentation robustness: independent visual failure analysis,” avoiding an invented causal relation to the interval-calibration work.
Input, GT, Prediction, and Error panels depict the same ring-shaped case; the error panel and linked ROI crops permit direct visual comparison.
The TP/FP/FN legend is adjacent to the error evidence, and the orange/red overlays correspond to missed-GT and prediction-only regions shown in the panels.
The medical-image content is specific and no audience-facing internal-process text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: Semantically coherent same-case segmentation comparison with an explicit independent-workstream transition.

observations: The contact sheet shows a coherent sequence: title/model, quantitative coverage result, simulation design, negative result, next experiment, then a visibly labeled independent segmentation analysis.
Adjacent slides vary composition substantially: equation/table, multi-panel line plot, workflow schematic, bar chart with interpretation, decision flow, and medical-image panel comparison.

The result → failure → next-experiment rhythm is visible across the coverage, small-G failure, and batch-selection slides; the intervening design slide provides useful context rather than redundant summary filler.

The deck avoids a repeated generic-card or one-template-page appearance. Density is generally balanced; the model slide is intentionally spacious around its central equation, while the later visual slides carry denser evidence.

CUHK identity is visually established in the title-page contact-sheet image through the university crest and “The Chinese University of Hong Kong” branding, and continued through the consistent Beamer header/footer styling.
No visible slide contains internal RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, workflow, repo-path, run-ID, or implementation-language leakage.
item_reviews.summary: A coherent, visually varied research-update deck with clear evidence-to-failure-to-next-step progression and a balanced independent workstream transition.

non_blocking_notes: Several plot labels and explanatory captions are necessarily small at contact-sheet scale, but the full-page rendered views show the principal chart elements and conclusions clearly.
